submitted.rationale: Index 10 (Ge 0.34, Mn2GeO4 stoichiometry; MEGNet HSE gap ~2.0 eV < 3.22 eV illumination, MACE near hull) gave the highest measured photocurrent, 1.5e-7 A, among the three merit measurements.

rejected.reason: MnGeO3 region measured 5e-8 A, lower than index 10
Mn-rich Mn2GeO4+Mn3O4 region measured 6e-8 A, lower than index 10
GeO2-rich; wide-gap GeO2 dilutes absorption; merit fell from Ge 0.34 to 0.50

consultations.verdict: Support: Mn2GeO4 (Ge 0.333) predicted HSE gap 2.0 eV (< 3.22 eV photon energy, absorbs) and near hull (0.055 eV/atom); index 10 (Ge 0.34) sits at this stoichiometry.
Support: MnGeO3 polymorph predicted gap 2.56 eV (other polymorph 2.1 eV), below 3.22 eV photon energy; index 19 (Ge 0.50) matches this stoichiometry and tests a distinct phase region from index 10.

Weak support: Mn-rich side of Mn2GeO4 should be a Mn2GeO4 + Mn3O4 (stable, on hull) mixture; the absorbing Mn2GeO4 phase gave the higher photocurrent so far and merit rose toward Mn-rich, so index 22 (Ge 0.23) tests that trend. MACE result on its own does not tell us much about merit.
